name: In llama.cpp, --tensor-split does not move MoE expert tensors, so a GPU split that looks configured is actually leaving expert compute on one device
symptom: Observable is a persistent asymmetry, not a crash or corruption: 'Even where --tensor-split doesn't cause degeneration, it barely rebalances actual per-GPU compute load: MoE experts stay almost entirely on one device regardless of the split ratio tried; only non-MoE tensors seem affected by the split value. --main-gpu had no effect on the imbalance either.' Observed alongside --n-cpu-moe 34 on Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q4_K_M with --split-mode layer --tensor-split 4,1.
root_cause: llama.cpp's split-mode row/layer logic distributes buffers according to their sizes, but expert tensors in an MoE checkpoint follow a placement rule that the tensor-split weighting does not drive, and --main-gpu is documented as a preference for the heaviest device rather than a forcing constraint. The result is that the split ratio a user tunes has almost no effect on where expert compute actually runs, so per-GPU utilization stays lopsided regardless of the setting.
workaround: Do not infer device placement from the --tensor-split value. Measure per-GPU utilization directly (nvidia-smi / rocm-smi during a real decode) to see where expert compute landed. Use --n-cpu-moe to control expert placement explicitly, and size the multi-GPU plan around the fact that expert weight is essentially fixed to one device unless offloaded.
notes: Same source as mgpu-llamacpp-tensor-split-breaks-nondivisible-multi-gpu-sharding and deliberately split out: that record is about the correctness symptom (output degeneration at long context), this one is about the persistent load imbalance which is a different mechanism and has a different fix. Recorded separately because the imbalance is present even in runs where output was correct, so the two never co-occur.
